clue.text: Girl's name I found in women's magazine

indicators.note: found in means the letter I is placed inside the magazine's name

parts.note: Elle is a well-known fashion magazine for women

explanation.surface: Someone spots a girl's name featured in the pages of a women's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl's name' reads as a single idea, but the definition is just 'Girl'; 'name' gives N and the 's is a link meaning 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nellie is a female first name, so it can stand for a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Old bar staff in Murphy's I almost forgot to visit

indicators.note: to visit means the PS goes in among the letters of the potatoes, calling on them

parts.note: a murphy is an informal word for a potato, and potatoes are taters
PS (postscript) is what you write when you almost forgot to say something

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the old barmen at Murphy's pub that they nearly forgot to drop in on.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy's looks like an Irish pub or stout; here a murphy is slang for a potato, so murphies are TATERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapster is an archaic word for a person who draws and serves beer in a tavern.

clue.text: King the writer's accepted by international Adriatic resort

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
the writer refers to the setter, so 'the writer is' becomes I'M
in means accepted, as in fashionable or let in

explanation.surface: A monarch with a famous author is welcomed at a seaside resort on the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a popular Italian beach town on the Adriatic coast.

clue.text: Doug likes eating fruit

indicators.note: eating means the words Doug likes swallow the answer, which is tucked inside them

explanation.surface: Doug enjoys eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Prick! Sackings extremely gratuitous

parts.note: a needle is something that pricks

indicators.note: extremely means take only the extreme letters of Sackings, its first and last

parts.note: its outer letters are S and S

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a boss whose sackings were wholly unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless and gratuitous both describe something done without any need or justification.

clue.text: Short note lawyer turned over eagerly? Perhaps

indicators.note: turned over means the combined letters are read in reverse order
short means the note is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a breve is a long musical note
DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: A brief memo was flipped over by a lawyer with keen interest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: 'eagerly' is one instance of the part of speech, and 'Perhaps' signals that.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagerly is a word modifying a verb, an example of this part of speech.

clue.text: Good doctor laid into King — he's always moaning

indicators.note: laid into means the doctor's letters are placed inside the king's

parts.note: a king is a ruler
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A decent physician attacked the monarch, who never stops complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' looks like a violent attack on the king, but it only signals one piece placed inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumbler is a person who constantly complains, which fits someone always moaning.

clue.text: Unfortunately get rain around start of afternoon (it might be good for lawn)

definitions.text: it might be good for lawn

indicators.note: around means the anagrammed letters go around the next piece
unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters of get rain are rearranged
start of means take just the first letter of afternoon

parts.note: its first letter is A

explanation.surface: A gardener's gripe about rain arriving in the afternoon, with an aside that it may benefit the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerating a lawn means piercing the soil so air reaches the roots, which helps the turf.

clue.text: Joiner's wife chopped tree

indicators.note: chopped means the wife's letter is cut from the word

parts.note: a welder joins metal, so is a joiner

explanation.surface: A carpenter's spouse cut down a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joiner' suggests a carpenter, but the joiner here is a WELDER.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a small tree or shrub bearing elderflowers and elderberries.

clue.text: Sensitive documents in a cellar — I'm satisfied that's improper

indicators.note: improper means not in the right state, so all these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds secret papers stored in a basement and is content that this is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified material is official information restricted to authorised people because it is secret.

clue.text: Retired programmer keeps book

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the hidden letters are read in reverse
keeps means the word programmer holds the letters inside it

explanation.surface: A computer programmer who has stopped working holds on to a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is Jane Austen's novel about a matchmaking heroine.

clue.text: Gradually becoming less safe in government

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Something dwindling while kept secure under official control.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is underworld slang for a safe; a safecracker is a peterman.
explanation.definitionFit: To peter out is to dwindle bit by bit until nothing is left.

clue.text: Ready to support German complaint

indicators.note: in a down clue, to support means to sit underneath, so the German letter goes on top

parts.note: ripe fruit is ready to eat

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared to back a German grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripe is an informal word for a grumble or grievance.

clue.text: Cycling award lost in middle of riot — flipping clots!

indicators.note: cycling means the letters rotate, the first going to the end

parts.note: the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: flipping means the combination is turned back to front
the clue word that signals this step
middle of means take the central letters of riot

parts.note: its middle letters are I and O
L is the abbreviation for lost, as in sports results tables

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at fools who lost an honour in the thick of a disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping clots' reads as a mild oath at fools, but flipping is the reversal signal and clots are blood clots.
explanation.definitionFit: Emboli are blood clots or other masses carried in the bloodstream that can block a vessel.

clue.text: Mike, Trump's behind crowd

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a behind is an ass, here the posterior of Trump

explanation.surface: A political jibe about Mike Pence standing behind Donald Trump among a throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass is a large body of people gathered together, a crowd.

clue.text: Around town main road sure to be closed completely

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, with the 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: around means the word for sure wraps itself about the town's letter

parts.note: right, as in 'right you are', means sure
T is the abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: Talk of a town's main road being definitely shut.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Airtight means sealed so no air can pass, i.e. shut tight.

clue.text: Said about half of the population's posts

indicators.note: said about means the word is spoken aloud and what we hear is a different spelling

parts.note: roughly half of all people are males

explanation.surface: Someone talking about the posts written by half the population.
explanation.definitionFit: To post a letter is to mail it, so posts as a verb equals mails.

clue.text: See 10
Doll keeps close to singer/songwriter

indicators.note: keeps means the doll's name holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: Ken is Barbie's boyfriend, a doll

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of singer

parts.note: its final letter is R

explanation.surface: A doll holding on to a singer-songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singer/songwriter' looks like one phrase; split it, the singer giving R and the songwriter being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jerome Kern was an American composer of musicals such as Show Boat.

clue.text: Source of money also in country raised capital

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the country's letters
in a down clue, raised means the letters read upwards, i.e. reversed

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
an ATM, a cash machine, is a source of money
and means also

explanation.surface: Money from a source within a country helped build up the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Katmandu, also spelled Kathmandu, is the capital city of Nepal.

clue.text: Old city bloke who's polite but desperate!

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
a gent is a courteous man, a gentleman

explanation.surface: A well-mannered man from an ancient city who is frantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Urgent and desperate both describe a need that demands immediate action.

clue.text: Boy (or girl) bringing up north regularly

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing up means moving the letter higher, i.e. earlier in the word

parts.note: Evelyn is a name given to both boys and girls

explanation.surface: A boy or girl raised in the north in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' sounds like raising a child; here it lifts the N two places up the column.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means at steady, equal intervals, which matches regularly.

clue.text: Spot coming out in troupe, dancing

indicators.note: dancing means moving around, so the letters of in troupe are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer's pimple appearing mid-performance in a dance company.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruption is a breaking out of a rash or pimple on the skin.

clue.text: Leading Republican has row causing great public anger

parts.note: up means ahead, as in a team leading by two
you row with an oar

explanation.surface: A senior Republican has a quarrel that triggers national fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' wants to be a quarrel, matching the anger; here it is the rowing sense, an OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An uproar is a loud collective outcry or protest from many people.

clue.text: Huge number of dogs slipping lead

indicators.note: slipping lead means losing the leading letter, as a dog slips its leash

parts.note: poodles are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Lots of dogs breaking free of their leashes.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, lots of something.

clue.text: Right to kill grass

parts.note: to ice is slang for to murder

explanation.surface: Someone claims an entitlement to destroy weeds in the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice is a cereal plant of the grass family, grown in paddy fields.

clue.text: Radiant Rod rocking but slowing down

indicators.note: rocking means moving to and fro, so the letters of Radiant Rod are rearranged

explanation.surface: A glowing rocker named Rod is performing, yet easing off the tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocking' suggests a musician playing rock; it is the anagram signal, and the musical tempo term is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritardando is the Italian musical direction for a gradual decrease in tempo.

clue.text: Shock! Guy's dropped first point

indicators.note: dropped first means the first occurrence of the point letter is removed

parts.note: to guy someone is to mock or tease them
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Surprise that Guy has lost the opening point of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a name, but it is the verb meaning to ridicule; TEASE loses its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: To tase is to stun with a Taser, an electroshock weapon.

clue.text: Prince William finally gets a game

parts.note: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of William

parts.note: its last letter is M

explanation.surface: Prince William at last gets to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prince William' looks like one royal; the prince is HAL and William just supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Halma is a board game in which pieces jump across a square board, an ancestor of Chinese chequers.

clue.text: Broadcast catches with fisherman

indicators.note: catches means the scattered word holds the other inside it

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter or strew it
and can mean with, as in fish and chips

explanation.surface: A radio show captures footage of an angler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' reads as radio or TV; here it is the old farming sense of scattering seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew the apostle was a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee before following Jesus.
